Nowy Targ Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowy Targ, Poland

Not demolished. Nowy Targ's Jewish community, first confirmed in the mid-17th century, reached 1,342 people (about 16 percent of the town) by 1921, most killed by the Germans in 1942. This cemetery, founded no later than 1869, holds the grave of Hasidic rabbi Jakow Jokil Hirsz (buried 1880), a student of Chaim Halberstam of Nowy Sącz, founder of the Sanz Hasidic dynasty. On August 30, 1942, the Germans shot between several hundred and 2,000 people at the cemetery, burying them in mass graves; the last person buried there was Dawid Grassgruen, shot and killed on February 10, 1946. In 2005, at the initiative of Rabbi Mendel Reichberg, a new tombstone commemorating Rabbi Hirsz was erected.
